articles.title: From restaurant guides to payments, here’s how TikTok is building a super app | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok announced this week that it’s adding an in-app restaurant guide, marking another step in the platform’s expansion beyond social media. The company has also recently been spotted developing a feature that would allow users to send money over direct messages.
The social media app has steadily expanded its offerings in recent years, adding TikTok Shop, a map for local discovery, more robust search features, games, and more. It appears that TikTok is taking steps to evolve into a “super app,” a single platform where users can do much more than just watch and share videos and that can actually handle a wide range of needs in one destination.
The super app model is big in China with apps like WeChat, which is kind of like Facebook, WhatsApp, Apple Pay, and an app store all rolled into a single platform. Of course, there’s the question of whether a super app model would work outside of China, but that doesn’t mean TikTok won’t try.
Instead of switching between apps, TikTok is working to become the app that people use for most of their digital activities. After taking its biggest leap with TikTok Shop, the company — which, notably, transitioned to new, primarily U.S. ownership back in January — has applied the same playbook to recent developments.
Restaurant Guides
TikTok has become a popular destination for restaurant recommendations, with viral videos often driving customers to local eateries. Now, the platform is looking to make that discovery process even easier with a new feature called “Must Eat.” The community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform.
“Must Eat” draws on more than 40 million posts and comments to compile restaurant recommendations and curated lists in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and narrow their search by cuisine, price, rating, and location.
The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. It also reflects how the app is expanding its role in users’ everyday decisions, from what they buy to where they choose to go out to eat.
Payments
Bloomberg reported in August that TikTok is developing a feature that would allow users to send each other money via direct messages. If rolled out, the feature would use the social media service’s TikTok Pay offering, which is already available in Southeast Asia for TikTok Shop purchases.
Additionally, Reuters reported in March that TikTok had applied to Brazil’s central bank for approval to operate as a financial technology company offering lending and payment services.
TikTok’s potential expansion into payments marks a significant way that the company is branching out beyond a social media platform and into a digital ecosystem. By aiming to bring financial services into its app, TikTok is looking to increase user engagement, open new revenue streams, and position itself to compete with fintech startups and e-commerce platforms.
Sports
Over the years, TikTok has steadily been looking to become a place where users can come for sports highlights and content. In early June, the company launched a dedicated hub for the FIFA World Cup where users can see scores, match schedules, standings, trending videos, highlights, videos from players, and more.
If people are already watching videos on TikTok but want to keep up with the score, they can do so without leaving the app or opening a dedicated sports news app or Google.
The World Cup hub was made possible through TikTok’s Sports-focused product called “TikTok GamePlan,” which is designed to allow sports teams, leagues, and broadcasters to drive discovery and engagement on the platform. The social media giant also has partnerships with Major League Soccer (MLS) and Major League Baseball (MLB) for behind-the-scenes and exclusive content.
Hotel and attraction booking
In May, TikTok launched TikTok GO, a way for users to discover and book hotels, attractions, and experiences directly within its app in the United States. TikTok GO surfaces lodging and things to do through videos, search, and location pages. When users find something they’re interested in, they can view details, check availability, and complete a booking.
Instead of directing users to third-party websites after they find a destination or recommendation in a video, TikTok has started positioning itself as a one-stop platform where viral travel content can drive bookings and revenue.
While people have already been using TikTok as a search engine and replacement for Google, this latest step puts TikTok in more direct competition with Google’s core businesses, Search and Google Maps, because it’s working to not only be the app where you discover places, but also the platform where you purchase that trip.
TikTok Shop
It’s widely known that one of TikTok’s biggest leaps beyond social media was the launch of TikTok Shop. TikTok began testing TikTok Shop in 2021 and launched it in the U.S. in 2023. Since then, the company has been able to successfully compete with Amazon, Shein, and other online marketplaces.
According to eMarketer, TikTok Shop grew its U.S. sales by 407% in 2024 and another 108% in 2025 to reach $15.82 billion. As of last year, the company accounted for 18.2% of total social commerce in the U.S., with that number expected to reach 24.1% by 2027.
Additionally, TikTok began challenging digital marketplaces even further with the launch of TikTok Shop gift cards late last year. TikTok Shop has also recently expanded into luxury retail, after initially mainly being known for cheap goods.
Music
TikTok’s popularity has influenced the music industry and how people discover new music, and the company tried to capitalize on this by launching a streaming service called TikTok Music in 2023 to take on platforms like Spotify and Apple Music, but ended up shutting it down a year later.
The company said it would focus on driving music listening and continue partnering with music streaming services rather than competing with them. TikTok hasn’t completely abandoned its music ambitions, however, as the company recently introduced a feature that lets Apple Music subscribers play full songs in the app after discovering them on their “For You” feed.
Search and Maps
TikTok has launched a robust search experience that surfaces maps, local hashtags, and even reviews to help users discover trending restaurants, travel locations, shops, and local experiences. It has also added more detailed information about places and restaurants on dedicated pages, allowing users to quickly see things like opening hours, star ratings, price ranges, and more.
TikTok was already eating into Google’s Search business when it first launched, as it quickly surfaced videos featuring commentary and visuals of restaurant food and places. However, users may still have needed to turn to Google Search to find a place’s exact location or to read reviews. Over the past few years, however, TikTok has increasingly eliminated that need by integrating detailed information about places right within its app.
Microdramas
While TikTok is known for user-generated entertainment, the company has also begun embracing microdramas by launching an in-app Minis section and a dedicated stand-alone app for bite-sized TV shows that can be watched in a series of one-minute episodes. While TikTok already competes with streaming giants like Netflix for users’ attention, its move into scripted shows puts it in even more direct competition with them.
It’s worth noting that TikTok first took strides into entertainment with the launch of livestreaming and support for longer videos, a significant move away from its initial focus on 15-second videos.
Games
TikTok has also launched a series of casual games in its app to get users to spend even more time on its platform and engage with others in DMs. The addition of games marked TikTok’s ongoing effort to go from a social media platform to an all-in-one entertainment platform where you can not only scroll through videos, but also challenge friends to easy-to-play games.

articles.title: Mượn 100 triệu của con gái, ông lão 72 tuổi gây đàn chồn 200 con, cá trê ‘dọn vệ sinh'
articles.text:
Khi trời vừa hửng sáng, ông Phạm Minh Châu (72 tuổi, ngụ phường Phước Thới, TP Cần Thơ) bóc vỏ từng trái chuối chín, chuẩn bị cho đàn chồn hương ăn. Công việc tưởng chừng đơn giản nhưng đòi hỏi người nuôi phải quan sát kỹ từng con, nhất là những con đang mang thai hoặc nuôi con non.
Khu trại rộng khoảng 200m2, với gần 200 ô chuồng được bố trí ngay ngắn. Bên trong, đàn chồn có nhiều lứa tuổi, từ những con trưởng thành nặng 5-6kg đến những con non mới tách mẹ.
Ít ai nghĩ rằng, người đàn ông đang thoăn thoắt chăm sóc đàn vật nuôi này chỉ mới bén duyên với nghề nuôi chồn từ năm 2024, khi đã bước sang tuổi 70.
Mượn tiền tiết kiệm của con gái để mua chồn giống
Trước khi nuôi chồn, ông Châu có hơn 20 năm làm nghề san lấp mặt bằng. Công việc vất vả, thường xuyên phải đi đây đó. Đến khi tuổi cao, ông nghĩ đến chuyện tìm một hướng đi mới để vừa có việc làm, vừa phát triển kinh tế gia đình.
Ông bắt đầu tìm hiểu mô hình sau một lần xem video trên YouTube, thấy nhiều người nuôi chồn hương đạt hiệu quả kinh tế cao. Có người cháu ở Cà Mau cũng đang nuôi chồn nên ông càng tò mò.
Không vội vàng đầu tư, ông dành nhiều thời gian xem các video hướng dẫn, đến những trang trại đã nuôi thành công để tham quan, học hỏi kinh nghiệm.
Sau khi xây dựng xong khu trại, ông tiếp tục chờ khoảng 6 tháng để tìm hiểu thêm trước khi quyết định mua con giống.
Đầu năm 2024, ông chính thức nuôi 5 con chồn hương, gồm 4 con cái và một con đực, mua tại trại giống ở tỉnh Vĩnh Long; đây là giống chồn Campuchia. Mỗi con giống có giá khoảng 20 triệu đồng, tổng số tiền đầu tư ban đầu 100 triệu đồng.
Ông cho hay đây vốn là tiền tiết kiệm gửi ngân hàng để dành cho con gái học đại học.
"Thời điểm đó không có sẵn tiền mặt, tôi nói với con gái cho cha mượn 100 triệu đồng để mua chồn nuôi. Tôi hứa cố gắng làm ăn, lo cho con ăn học. Con gái nghe xuôi tai, gật đầu đồng ý, tôi mới rút tiền đi mua 5 con giống", ông Châu kể. Ông còn vay thêm 50 triệu đồng từ nguồn vốn chính sách để đầu tư chuồng trại.
Những ngày đầu nuôi chồn hương, ông không khỏi lo lắng. Tuy nhiên, nhờ chịu khó học hỏi và được những người nuôi trước hướng dẫn, ông dần nắm được kỹ thuật chăm sóc.
Đến tháng 9/2024, những con chồn cái đầu tiên bắt đầu sinh sản. Mỗi lứa thường sinh 3-4 con, cá biệt có con sinh 5-6 con. Nhận thấy đàn chồn phát triển tốt, ông giữ lại những con cái khỏe mạnh để làm giống, từng bước nhân đàn.
Nuôi cá trê dưới chuồng chồn để giảm công vệ sinh
Trong quá trình nuôi chồn hương, ông Châu nhận ra một trong những khâu tốn công nhất là vệ sinh chuồng trại. Chồn hương thích ăn thức ăn tươi sống nhưng nơi ở phải luôn sạch sẽ, khô ráo.
Ban đầu nuôi trên nền xi măng, ngày nào ông Châu cũng phải quét dọn, dội rửa cực nhọc.
Sau một thời gian suy nghĩ, ông Châu nghĩ ra cách làm độc đáo: tận dụng ngay diện tích dưới sàn chuồng chồn để nuôi cá trê. Lúc đầu sợ nuôi cá trong nhà thiếu ánh sáng cá không sống nổi, ông đóng ô ván, lót bạt rồi thả thử 10kg cá trê giống.
Thấy cá phát triển tốt sau 3 tháng, ông mạnh dạn cắt nền gạch, đào sâu xuống làm hệ thống hồ chìm dài 10-12m, rộng 2m lót gạch kiên cố để nuôi lâu dài.
"Toàn bộ chất thải và thức ăn rơi vãi của chồn ở tầng trên rớt xuống làm thức ăn cho cá trê ở tầng dưới. Cách này giúp chuồng trại luôn khô ráo, không có mùi hôi, chồn ít bị bệnh mà tôi cũng đỡ tốn công dọn dẹp. Cứ 5-7 ngày thay nước hồ cá một lần là xong", ông Châu chia sẻ. Đàn cá trê phát triển tốt và được tận dụng làm nguồn thức ăn cho chồn.
Chuồng chồn được làm bằng lưới kẽm ô vuông, sàn bằng inox, kích thước mỗi ô rộng khoảng 60cm, dài 80cm. Toàn bộ khu nuôi được bố trí thành từng dãy để thuận tiện theo dõi, chăm sóc và quản lý đàn.
Theo ông, nuôi chồn không quá phức tạp nếu người nuôi chú ý ba yếu tố: thức ăn, nước uống và vệ sinh chuồng trại.
Về chế độ dinh dưỡng, ông áp dụng công thức "sáng nhẹ - chiều no". Sáng cho ăn chuối chín; chiều khoảng 16h cho ăn 150g thức ăn hỗn hợp gồm chuối, cá hoặc ếch xay nhuyễn trộn cùng thức ăn chăn nuôi.
Riêng những con chồn mẹ đang nuôi con, ông chủ động tăng lượng thức ăn để bảo đảm dinh dưỡng. Từ đó, đàn chồn giống Campuchia tăng trọng nhanh.
Sau những lứa sinh sản đầu tiên, đàn chồn ngày càng phát triển. Từ 5 con giống ban đầu, đến nay khu trại có khoảng 200 con, trong đó hàng chục con bố mẹ, còn lại là chồn hậu bị và chồn con. Với chồn hương, sau khoảng 10 tháng tuổi có thể bắt đầu phối giống.
Thời gian mang thai khoảng 60 ngày, mỗi lứa thường sinh 3-6 con. Ông hạn chế can thiệp vào quá trình nuôi con của chồn mẹ. Khi chồn sinh sản, ông để con mẹ tự chăm sóc con non, chỉ chú ý cung cấp đủ thức ăn, nước uống và giữ môi trường chuồng sạch sẽ.
Ông Châu hiện chủ yếu bán chồn giống, hạn chế bán chồn thịt. Ông cho hay, giá chồn thịt dao động khoảng 1,2-1,3 triệu đồng/kg. Chồn thương phẩm thường được thương lái lựa chọn ở mức trọng lượng 2,8-4 kg/con.
Đối với chồn giống, giá bán tùy thuộc vào độ tuổi, trọng lượng và khả năng sinh sản. Chồn con đã biết ăn, nặng 1kg, có giá khoảng 7 triệu đồng/cặp đực - cái. Những cặp giống trưởng thành, có thể phối giống, giá khoảng 15-20 triệu đồng/cặp.
Theo ông Châu, doanh thu từ bán chồn giống đạt hơn 250 triệu đồng. Thời gian tới, ông sẽ giữ lại những con giống tốt để tăng đàn.
Không chỉ mang lại nguồn thu, khu trại của ông còn trở thành nơi để một số người dân tìm đến tham quan, học hỏi kinh nghiệm.
Ông Nguyễn Thiện Nhân, Phó Chủ tịch Hội Nông dân phường Phước Thới, đánh giá mô hình nuôi chồn hương của ông Châu là hướng sản xuất mới, bước đầu mang lại hiệu quả kinh tế, tạo điều kiện để người dân địa phương học hỏi, phát triển chăn nuôi. Mô hình này đã được công nhận đạt chứng nhận dân vận khéo cấp phường.
Ông cho biết địa phương sẵn sàng đồng hành, hỗ trợ ông Châu tiếp cận nguồn vốn nếu có nhu cầu mở rộng sản xuất.

articles.title: How building a cheap home server could save you money in the long run - Engadget
articles.text:
How building a cheap home server could save you money in the long run
That hunk of plastic collecting dust in the basement might be more useful than you realized.
Being around technology or computers for any extended period of time means that you've likely accumulated a decent amount of hardware over the years. With new upgrades and changes to one's setup often comes a question about what to do with old stuff you don't use anymore, or what you can do with any new hardware you get your hands on.
It's a common question regarding what to do with old PCs or laptops, but one that has a few surprising answers. One that always springs to mind is the creation of a home server, which, if you're a family looking to build your own custom streaming hub or have your own free mass storage unit, is a fabulous bit of financial investment that could be immensely beneficial to you in the uncertain years ahead of us in the technology field.
Building a home server is also tantalizingly easy, as well, making the entire process one that is both painless and affordable. And in a time when things feel a bit more complex than they should, having something as straightforward as the construction of a media server that could save you money honestly feels like a slam dunk.
It can trim down your streaming services bill
In addition to your regular bills, one thing that most of us spend a lot of money on during each calendar month is streaming services. There are a lot of them, and nearly every major company in the world has decided to put a plus symbol next to its name in order to enter the streaming service arms race.
It can add up to quite a bit of money over four weeks, and one way to combat that is to build your own home server. With one of these at your disposal, your server becomes something of a custom media machine, where you can stream your own shows and movies as you please. It can greatly cut down on the number of streaming services you have, making things a little lighter on your wallet.
It's sometimes shocking to see how many streaming services a family of any size is subscribed to, and using a home server to offset that can really help you keep your monthly bill down to a more manageable number. Thanks to media servers like Plex, Jellyfin and countless other alternatives, you can populate your device with anything you want.
Great cost-cutting measures on mass storage
Huge parts of our personal lives are often stored in our digital archives, as so many of us have precious photos and videos logged on our devices. If you're someone who has a fairly hefty selection of files, or even just incredibly important documents, a home server can pull its weight by doubling as a mass storage device.
If you subscribe to any sort of cloud storage or data backup service, it can all start to add up over the year. With your own home server, you can cut those elements out, and the server itself can also be upgradeable over time. If you're ever in need of more storage, the act of buying more hard drives and installing them is a snap.
By resurrecting an old PC that's seen its last days as a daily, primary driver into a home server, you can save a fairly large chunk of cash on storage and home entertainment needs. It can also act as a sort of building block toward actual custom PC builds, and once you have a strong understanding of those things, you may find that you have quite a bit of extra cash in your account every month.

articles.title: I took two iPhones on vacation. The Duo won me over. | TechCrunch
articles.text:
“I think I’m going to switch back to my other iPhone.”
I’ll admit, I said this multiple times during my five-day vacation with the new iPhone Duo, after encountering frustrations with broken apps, unfamiliar gestures (a return to Touch ID, argh!), and camera concerns that had me lugging around two phones.
By the time the trip was over, I didn’t want to go back.
When I first unboxed the Duo, a loaner from Apple, I was genuinely intrigued. I felt a flutter of anticipation as I peeled back the factory seal wrap and booted up the device. In retrospect, this was probably the first signal that Duo was going to ultimately win me over.
As a tech reporter, I’ve received a lot of test devices over the years, so unfortunately, opening a package with a new gadget inside is no longer the thrill it used to be. But sometime in the days leading up to the Duo’s ship date, I found myself actually wanting one – I had started doing the math and comparing upgrade options that would allow me to afford the $2K the phone would cost. I started scrolling TikTok reviews of Duo cases. I hesitated not only because of the price but because moving to the Duo is a major change – especially coming from an iPhone 17 Pro Max. The phones could not be more different.
As I was about to head out on vacation when the Duo arrived, I decided to tote my 17 Pro Max with me too, as something of a safety net. I ended up using the Duo more, and grew comfortable with it over the course of the trip, despite some frustrations.
There’s always a psychological switching cost in changing phones, but particularly going from a high-end phone to a more experimental device like the Duo. For someone used to the iPhone’s long-perfected tech and thin rectangular shape, the Duo’s short, squat, and decidedly novel nature was somewhat off-putting at first.
“Where is all that screen real estate I used to have?” I lamented. “Will this thing even fit comfortably in my pocket?”
As it turns out, it does. Front and back pockets, in fact. Even while wearing a case. You can sit down with it in your back pocket, effectively squashing it, and it does not break. (I meant to be more careful, but I forgot to be, repeatedly, as I tend to carry phones in my back pocket when walking around. I sat on the phone countless times. It’s clearly not that fragile.)
I also dropped the phone (by accident!) at least three times. Twice from about table height and once when it got pushed off the side of the bed. It did not fall on soft carpet, but rather on concrete, tile, and wood floors. It didn’t break then either, and the screen didn’t crack. I wouldn’t call these professional drop tests by any means, but it certainly was a relief for someone fairly clumsy with their phone.
Of course, I did encounter some frustrations. I had to scroll more to read back through text threads because of the Duo’s small outer screen; unoptimized apps with numerous controls sometimes had key features tucked away in a “more” (three-dot) menu, leading to a hunt to find the option you needed; and, on multiple occasions, the Google Search app just froze.
Though not Apple’s fault, the latter turned out to be my biggest annoyance software-wise, given that Search is one of my go-to apps especially when traveling. On vacation, I open the app repeatedly to look up points of interest, restaurant reviews, distances between towns, weather, and more. But Google’s app would just stop working, and tapping its back button did nothing.
This seemed to be a problem specific to the Search app’s AI Mode, which these days you’re often dropped into without actually requesting it. (Even more reason to be annoyed by AI Search!) The workaround has been to force-close the app, so the next time you open it, your returned to the home screen with the search box. (It amazes me that, in a time when Google is facing a search decline because of AI, it wouldn’t have prioritized making its Search app functional on Apple’s latest device!)
In addition, many of the early reviews pointed out how many apps were not updated or redesigned for Duo at launch, which meant they had a telltale black bar on the side, cramping the limited screen real estate when the phone is closed even further. This is true, but personally speaking, I didn’t think it was a dealbreaker for making a switch to the Duo.
For one thing, companies have been pushing out their Duo-optimized updates fairly quickly. Those that have not – and there are still more than a few! – continue to be usable. They’re just kind of … ugly.
Google Maps was not Duo-optimized during the trip, yet I had no problem using it for driving directions, local search and discovery, route planning, and the like. If anything, the black-barred apps felt more like an aesthetic issue than a functional problem, even though they’re smaller than usual when the Duo is folded.
I expect all the major apps will eventually update. As for the older apps that never do? Well, it’s probably time to move on from apps no longer being maintained, I’d say, particularly in an era when older software is being exploited left and right by AI-enabled hacking tools.
However, I will agree with the other reviewers who complained about the lack of Face ID.
This is the Duo’s biggest drawback – not the screen, not the camera, not the lack of an Action button for launching your preferred AI assistant. It’s Touch ID.
It is much easier to look at your phone than to fiddle around with finger presses. While I easily avoided the need to use Touch ID to unlock the device – I am almost always wearing an Apple Watch, which serves as an alternative authentication method – I often stumbled when it came to using apps and Apple Pay.
Tap-and-pay is one of the areas where it’s immediately obvious how much smoother Face ID has made everyday tasks. Returning to Touch ID at the time of payment was cumbersome, given that you’re often holding shopping bags, a purse, and, in my case, a dog leash, in addition to the phone you’re using to pay with.
There’s a certain amount of what I guess I’ll call “muscle memory” that you have to overcome when you switch back to Touch ID. I found the easiest grip was to cradle the phone in your hand and use your thumb to authenticate. But where I repeatedly messed up was remembering to keep my thumb or finger on the Touch ID sensor long enough to authenticate. At times, my finger wasn’t situated quite right (I blame the dog pulling on the leash!), and I had to readjust. “I miss Face ID!,” I complained multiple times at checkout.
Though returning to Touch ID was something I got used to, it’s far from ideal. I can see this as being a real stopping point for some early adopters who would otherwise want to move to the Duo. It’s not an insurmountable problem, but it’s among the top reasons not to get the Duo now, in my opinion. (A future version is said to support Face ID.)
Another reason to be wary of the Duo? The camera. Much has been said about the Duo’s lesser camera system. The Duo has two rear cameras to my iPhone 17 Pro Max’s three. It has no telephoto lens. It has a 10x digital zoom versus the Pro’s 40x. The Pro has more advanced hardware for low-light photography and supports ProRAW, ProRes, and other advanced features.
Very simply put: if you are an iPhone photographer or a content creator, you shouldn’t consider the Duo as your primary device.
For, you know, us normal folks, the Duo’s camera is okay. Not great, but fine. What were you going to do with those photos you’re snapping anyway? Post them to Instagram Stories or Facebook? Text them to a friend? Look back on them fondly when they reappear in your photo widget on your Home Screen? Turn them into a Lock Screen wallpaper? None of these things requires a Pro-level camera.
Below are a few photos shot with the Duo versus others shot with the 17 Pro Max. None of the photos are using any special settings or filters; they are intentionally just average, non-professional point-and-shoot shots. Among my complaints are that the Duo’s image processing can, at times, make fine details, like the leaves on trees, look overprocessed. Meanwhile, distant landscapes can appear flatter or smoothed over — though, to be fair, the Blue Ridge Mountains are naturally hazy, so it’s hard to say how much of that is the camera. (Shots from the mountaintop were in low-light conditions — it was getting dark out.)
DUO PHOTOS:
PRO MAX PHOTOS:
As for why to get the phone? This one’s easy; it’s a foldable. From Apple. First, foldables are whimsical in a way that slab phones will never be. They are toys for grown-ups! Developers are also clearly having fun building for the new format, so there are lots of new apps to play with. Plus, it’s a great way to watch movies, particularly with that Duo Folio case with a kickstand.
Second, it’s a foldable from Apple. The company has taken its time to get it right, which comes through in the details, from the barely visible crease to the consistent aspect ratio between screens, allowing content to scale proportionally. It’s also a foldable in Apple’s software ecosystem, which matters for those who move between Apple devices and services and who use and pay for apps that are designed for iOS specifically.
But here’s a small confession: in day-to-day life, I didn’t unfold the Duo as much as I thought I would. (To be clear: I absolutely did unfold it! I just thought I would do it more!)
There are two reasons for this. One: unfolding the device in public invites conversation, and it feels sort of like a flex; I’m not always in a place where I have time to chat. I expect this problem to diminish in time as the novelty wears off.
That said, I still had roughly half a dozen conversations with strangers while I was on vacation, from fellow shoppers to servers to business owners. I even handed them the device at times (when they couldn’t easily run off with it!) and let them fold and unfold it. One person wanted to see the Kid Cue feature in particular, which displays playful Snoopy animations on the phone’s outer display to get children to look toward the camera when you take their picture. They were genuinely delighted by this.
Anecdotally, the consensus was that the unfolded screen was something of a marvel to most: “You can’t see the hinge!” “Is that a screen protector or is it just like that?” (The inner screen has a matte, nano-texture finish, reducing glare. Once explained, it was also praised as “pretty cool.” )
“What if you get sand in it?,” a former Samsung Galaxy Fold owner asked. Their older Android foldable had been ruined after a trip to the beach where sand got into the hinge, causing damage to the screen. (This was not uncommon at the time.) The Duo is rated IP68, the “6” signifying higher dust resistance, making it dust-tight. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 was rated IP48, by comparison. I’m not expecting it will have the same issues, though I do hope a reviewer takes it to the beach soon!
I am certain that at least one of the handful of strangers I spoke to had never actually seen a phone that folded before. The fact that Apple has now made one means this concept will no longer be niche; it will be known to the mainstream.
The other reason I didn’t unfold it as much as I thought is that doing so feels like the start of a more intentional screen time session. When I do unfold the phone now, it’s because I’m truly engaging with what I’m doing on the phone, like watching a show on Netflix or dragging two apps side-by-side in split-screen mode for multitasking. (I love reading news in Inoreader and having X open off to the side to see what people are saying about the news, but that’s a use case that won’t apply to everyone!)
The split-screen feature is easy to use, too – with the app open, you swipe up from the bottom, then drag it to the left or right edge. Target boxes on each side help you visualize where it can move to, which is helpful. (You can also long-press on an app icon to open a split view, but I don’t do this as much.)
But as something of a “mini” phone in terms of screen size when closed, I’m somehow less drawn to what I think of as time-wasting apps like TikTok, Instagram, or casual games.
I’ve been thinking about this, and I don’t believe it’s just the lack of screen real estate when the phone is folded, or the fact that vertical apps haven’t been designed for the Duo’s unfolded landscape screen. Those concerns make sense from a practical, usability standpoint, of course, but there’s something more to this behavioral change, I believe.
For years, phones have been getting bigger, taller, thinner, and more comfortable to hold. Consequently, they easily sucked us into their digital worlds. With the Duo, the design seems to interrupt the way smartphones effortlessly pull us in, begging us to open apps and scroll endlessly.
Rather, the Duo feels like a device you open and use when you have reason to do so, not something you reflexively turn to when you’re bored or have a few minutes to spare. Because the best app use cases are when the phone is unfolded, and unfolding is something you do with careful consideration (and careful hands!), device use becomes more thoughtful.
This is not a bad thing. It also aligns with the embrace of retro tech already underway, where knobs and dials and buttons make engaging with technology feel more deliberate.
And for that reason, despite its faults, the Duo won me over. It’s a phone that’s compelling and fun — a phone I enjoyed picking up, but also found easier to put down.

articles.title: Elon Musk “troll” vụ Binance bị hack, CZ nói thẳng: “Tôi rất tôn trọng anh, làm ơn hãy dừng lại”
articles.text:
Đồng sáng lập Binance đề nghị tỷ phú Mỹ ngừng chế giễu sàn và “ủng hộ một chút”, đồng thời nhắc rằng Binance đang nắm cổ phần trị giá hơn 1 tỷ USD tại SpaceX.
Đồng sáng lập kiêm cựu CEO Binance Changpeng Zhao (CZ) hôm 30/10 đã công khai đề nghị Elon Musk ngừng “troll” công ty, sau khi CEO SpaceX và Tesla đăng một loạt biểu tượng cảm xúc có vẻ chế nhạo vụ tấn công mạng nhằm vào sàn tiền điện tử lớn nhất thế giới.
Binance bị hack với thiệt hại 6,3 tỷ USD vào cuối ngày 29/10. Khi thông tin lan ra, Musk đăng nhiều biểu tượng cảm xúc trên mạng xã hội X, từ cười lớn đến nhăn nhó.
Đáp lại, CZ nhắc Musk về mối quan hệ lợi ích giữa hai bên. Theo ông, cổ phần của Binance tại SpaceX, bắt nguồn từ khoản đầu tư trước đây vào Twitter, hiện trị giá hơn 1 tỷ USD. Con số này chỉ là một phần rất nhỏ so với mức định giá khoảng 2.000 tỷ USD của SpaceX.
“Elon, tôi rất tôn trọng anh, nhưng giờ không phải lúc để troll. Làm ơn dừng lại”, CZ viết trên X lúc 9h19 sáng (giờ miền Đông nước Mỹ). “Cổ phiếu SPCX của chúng tôi (từ khoản đầu tư 500 triệu USD vào thương vụ mua lại Twitter của anh) hiện trị giá hơn một tỷ USD. Mong anh ủng hộ chúng tôi một chút. Cảm ơn!”
Bài đăng của CZ thu hút 27,4 nghìn lượt thích và 3,8 nghìn lượt trả lời tại thời điểm bài viết được đăng.
Đây không phải lần đầu CZ và Musk công kích nhau trên mạng. Tháng 11/2021, Binance tạm ngừng cho rút Dogecoin vì lỗi ví, và Musk gọi động thái này là “mờ ám”. Khi đó, CZ đáp trả bằng cách nhắc đến đợt triệu hồi lớn của Tesla với gần 12.000 xe tại Mỹ do lỗi phần mềm và phần cứng.
Tham khảo: CNBC

articles.title: Your Family Will Adore These Smart String Lights
articles.text:
The holiday season is creeping closer, and one way to create the right atmosphere is to snag some smart string lights. They’re perfect for the tree, but you can also use them as outdoor lighting around your porch or hang them on furniture to cozy up a room. Govee offers a frankly astounding lineup of smart lighting, backed by perhaps the most feature-packed app, so it’s a great choice if you want to light up your life.
The Govee Christmas Lights 2, the budget pick in our best smart Christmas lights guide, are already relatively affordable, but a further 25 percent discount is not to be sniffed at. You can get $25 off the 66-foot length, perfect for the average tree, all the way up to $100 off the 328-foot length to cover your entire front yard. I haven’t seen them priced this low since Black Friday last year.
These string lights are IP67 rated and can withstand extreme temperatures, so you can use them just about anywhere. That said, you’ll need an outdoor outlet, and if you aim to get a good outdoor lighting display going, I recommend a weatherproof electrical box.
The string itself is green, so it blends in perfectly with a real or fake indoor Christmas tree or any real outdoor trees or shrubs. The spool makes it easy to unravel the string and get them installed. You can connect them via Bluetooth or Wi-Fi and use the Govee app, or add them to your smart home ecosystem of choice via Matter. There’s a little control unit with a power button, but you’ll want to connect them to your smart home for remote control and automatic scheduling.
While it may take you a few minutes to get your head around, I recommend using the Govee app because it is packed full of fun features. At the shallow end, you can change the color and brightness of the lights, but there’s so much more to it than that. By mapping your lights using your phone camera, you can select complex animated lighting effects. There are well over 100 presets to choose from, but you can also have the app generate effects for you based on your interests.
They may have Christmas in the name, but these string lights are so versatile that you can find effects to suit any scenario, from spooky Halloween animations to classy white light that works year-round. I've used these outdoors for a couple of years now, and they’re still going strong.

articles.title: Why your Spotify might be using so much storage - Engadget
articles.text:
Why your Spotify might be using so much storage
If you're running low on storage, it's worth checking to see if Spotify might be the culprit.
We're all getting tired of subscription-based services, but when it comes to music streaming, it's a little harder to give up. You can still purchase individual tracks and albums, but it's often more economical to subscribe to Apple Music or Spotify if you listen to a wide variety of music. Furthermore, with how fast and reliable mobile data has become, you can stream virtually any song you want on the go. This saves you the hassle of managing a local library of music on your phone, not to mention the storage space you could otherwise use for other apps and media files.
If you've recently been hit by the low-storage warning on your phone, you can find out exactly what's taking up so much space. On iOS, navigate to Settings > General > iPhone Storage. If you're using Android, the exact menu labels may vary depending on your phone's manufacturer, and the easiest way to find this information may be to simply search your phone for "Storage." For Samsung, look under Settings > Device care > Storage. For other Android devices, you can usually locate it under Settings > Storage or Settings > About Phone > Storage. Your phone might automatically sort your apps by how much storage they're occupying. If you spot Spotify near the top, there's a good chance that downloaded music or cached data is what's eating away at your phone's storage.
Android lets you clear an app's cache in just a few taps. Navigate to something like Settings > Apps > See all apps > Spotify > Storage & cache and tap on Clear cache. Though you can nuke your entire offline music library by tapping on the Clear storage button, this will also sign you out of the app. Instead, the Spotify app offers a much better way to manage your downloads.
Manage your Spotify downloads
In the Spotify app on Android and iOS, you can check what music you have downloaded by navigating to the Your Library tab and tapping on Downloaded at the top. Here, you can pick individual playlists or albums and tap on the green download button to remove them from your device. This is a good way to free up storage by deleting the songs you don't want available offline, while keeping the stuff you do listen to more frequently.
You can, however, delete all downloads if you want to reclaim as much storage on your phone as possible. In the Spotify app, tap on your profile picture in the top-left corner of the screen. Navigate to Settings and privacy > Data-saving and offline, scroll all the way down and tap on Remove next to the Remove all downloads option. You can also clear Spotify's cache here.
You might need to restart your phone if you don't immediately see the freed-up storage reflected in your phone's settings. Other streaming services like Apple Music and Netflix also let you remove downloads — you just have to look for the option within the app's settings.
If you're using the Spotify app on a Windows or macOS computer, you can clear downloads by clicking on your profile picture, navigating to Settings, scrolling all the way down to the Storage section and clicking on Remove all downloads. Those who use Spotify on the web shouldn't have to worry about downloads taking up device storage, since the browser version doesn't support offline listening to begin with.
Adjust media quality on Spotify
If you do need an offline music library so you can listen to your tracks without an internet connection, you can still clear some storage space by adjusting the quality of your downloaded songs. On Android and iOS, launch Spotify and head to Settings and privacy > Media quality and scroll to the Download quality section. You can choose the Low option, then tap on the Download button next to the Update existing downloads option. Spotify says tracks downloaded or streamed in the Low quality setting are equivalent to around 24 kbps, which shouldn't be too bad for casual listening.
It's also worth noting that if you have the Lossless quality preset selected for your downloads, your offline music library is going to occupy significantly more storage. Lossless tracks are much larger than their compressed counterparts. While lossless audio can upgrade your music listening experience if you're using wired headphones and a DAC, the difference might not be noticeable if you usually opt for wireless earbuds.
I tested just how big of a difference downloading the same set of songs in different quality presets can make. With my music library downloaded in Lossless quality, Spotify was occupying around 22GB of space on my phone. When set to the Low preset, my entire music library fit in a little over 2GB — those are massive storage savings, and I didn't even have to give up offline listening. Periodically clearing Spotify's cache can also free up a noticeable amount of storage space.

articles.title: Kính mắt Anna đặt mục tiêu nhân đôi hệ thống vào năm 2028
articles.text:
Từ dấu mốc kỷ lục đến chiến lược phát triển quy mô
Tháng 8/2026, Kính mắt Anna, thuộc Công ty Cổ phần ALC Phú Quý, được Tổ chức Kỷ lục Việt Nam (VietKings) trao bằng chứng nhận “Thương hiệu kính mắt có hệ thống cửa hàng lớn nhất Việt Nam”. Tại thời điểm được ghi nhận, thương hiệu có 75 cửa hàng hiện diện tại 27/34 tỉnh, thành phố.
Dấu mốc này phản ánh quá trình phát triển mạng lưới bán lẻ của Anna, đồng thời tạo nền tảng cho kế hoạch mở rộng trong giai đoạn tiếp theo. Thay vì chỉ tập trung vào việc gia tăng số lượng điểm bán, thương hiệu hướng đến xây dựng hệ thống có khả năng phục vụ khách hàng xuyên suốt từ khâu lựa chọn sản phẩm, tư vấn thị lực đến hỗ trợ sau mua.
Đối với ngành hàng kính mắt, trải nghiệm trực tiếp vẫn là một phần quan trọng trong quyết định mua sắm. Người dùng cần thử nhiều kiểu gọng để tìm được thiết kế phù hợp, được tư vấn về tròng kính theo nhu cầu và tiếp cận các dịch vụ đo khám khi cần thiết. Vì vậy, mạng lưới cửa hàng rộng khắp có thể tạo thêm thuận tiện cho khách hàng, đặc biệt khi nhu cầu mua sắm và chăm sóc kính phát sinh trong quá trình sử dụng.
Theo định hướng của Anna, hệ thống cửa hàng được phát triển theo phong cách hiện đại, trẻ trung, kết hợp danh mục gọng kính đa dạng và các dịch vụ hỗ trợ thị lực. Cách tiếp cận này hướng đến việc đáp ứng đồng thời nhu cầu sử dụng kính trong sinh hoạt hằng ngày và nhu cầu thể hiện phong cách cá nhân của người tiêu dùng.
Lấy trải nghiệm khách hàng làm trọng tâm khi mở rộng hệ thống
Khi quy mô chuỗi bán lẻ ngày càng lớn, thách thức không chỉ nằm ở việc mở thêm cửa hàng mà còn ở khả năng duy trì chất lượng phục vụ tại từng điểm bán. Đặc biệt với sản phẩm liên quan trực tiếp đến thị lực, trải nghiệm khách hàng phụ thuộc vào nhiều yếu tố, từ năng lực tư vấn, quy trình đo khám đến khả năng hỗ trợ kỹ thuật sau khi mua.
Theo chính sách được thương hiệu công bố, khách hàng được miễn phí đo khám mắt, vệ sinh và nắn chỉnh kính trọn đời. Đối với sản phẩm gặp lỗi từ nhà sản xuất, Anna áp dụng chính sách bảo hành 1 đổi 1 theo các điều kiện bảo hành tương ứng.
Những chính sách này hướng đến việc duy trì sự đồng hành với khách hàng sau giao dịch, thay vì giới hạn trải nghiệm ở thời điểm mua sản phẩm. Khi có nhu cầu vệ sinh kính, điều chỉnh gọng hoặc xử lý các vấn đề phát sinh trong quá trình sử dụng, khách hàng có thêm cơ hội tiếp cận dịch vụ hỗ trợ tại hệ thống cửa hàng.
Tuy nhiên, để triển khai nhất quán trên quy mô lớn, doanh nghiệp cần chú trọng đào tạo nhân sự, hoàn thiện quy trình vận hành và kiểm soát chất lượng dịch vụ. Đây là những yếu tố có ý nghĩa đối với khả năng duy trì trải nghiệm đồng đều khi số lượng cửa hàng tiếp tục gia tăng.
Song song với dịch vụ, danh mục sản phẩm cũng là một phần trong định hướng phát triển của Anna. Thương hiệu chú trọng cập nhật các thiết kế gọng kính theo xu hướng, đa dạng kiểu dáng và kết hợp tư vấn nhằm giúp khách hàng lựa chọn sản phẩm phù hợp với nhu cầu sử dụng, đặc điểm khuôn mặt và phong cách riêng.
Tham vọng 150 cửa hàng và bài toán tăng trưởng bền vững
Trên nền tảng hệ thống 75 cửa hàng hiện có, Kính mắt Anna đặt mục tiêu nâng quy mô mạng lưới lên 150 điểm bán vào năm 2028. Nếu hoàn thành kế hoạch, số lượng cửa hàng của thương hiệu sẽ tăng gấp đôi so với thời điểm xác lập kỷ lục vào tháng 8/2026.
Kế hoạch này thể hiện tham vọng mở rộng sự hiện diện của Anna trên thị trường kính mắt Việt Nam, đồng thời tăng khả năng tiếp cận sản phẩm và dịch vụ tại nhiều khu vực. Việc phát triển mạng lưới cũng mở ra yêu cầu tiếp tục hoàn thiện mô hình quản trị chuỗi, từ lựa chọn địa điểm, tổ chức nhân sự đến kiểm soát chất lượng sản phẩm và chính sách hậu mãi.
Trong bối cảnh thị trường bán lẻ ngày càng chú trọng trải nghiệm thực tế, khả năng kết hợp giữa độ phủ hệ thống và chất lượng phục vụ sẽ là yếu tố đáng quan tâm đối với các thương hiệu lựa chọn chiến lược tăng trưởng bằng mạng lưới cửa hàng.
Từ cột mốc 75 cửa hàng tại 27 tỉnh, thành phố đến mục tiêu 150 điểm bán vào năm 2028, Kính mắt Anna đang từng bước mở rộng quy mô hoạt động. Chặng đường tiếp theo không chỉ được đo bằng số lượng cửa hàng mới mà còn ở khả năng đưa trải nghiệm mua sắm và dịch vụ chăm sóc thị lực đến gần hơn với người tiêu dùng trên toàn quốc.

articles.title: There’s a Completely New Type of Whisky. It’s French and Made in Concrete Eggs
articles.text:
The vines on Bordeaux’s Right Bank next to the Dordogne were first planted by Roman troops and settlers in the first century CE. Known for Merlot-dominant blends, with its clay and limestone soils, this region of France delivers softer, fruitier wines. If you're a fan of Pomerol or St-Émilion, this is your nirvana.
It is here you will find Maison Lineti, happily shunning 2,000 years of tradition by making not wine, but whisky. French whisky. A thousand miles or so from the distilleries of Scotland and Ireland, this small company is making the spirit in a way whisky has never been made before.
Even though Maison Lineti is not making wine, it is, in what is apparently a world first, applying wine-science methods to fermentation, distillation, and maturation for its whisky. The result is a floral, fresh, mineral, and textured spirit.
After the producer hosted the prestigious World Whisky Forum in June 2025, its methods have set the industry all aflutter. Why? Not only does the product taste exceptional, Lineti's groundbreaking techniques are bringing its spirit to the bottle years faster than traditional players using traditional processes.
The masterminds behind Maison Lineti's wine-made whisky are Magali Picard, a chemical engineer who holds a doctorate in oenology from the University of Bordeaux, and her partner and cofounder, Alex Cosculluela. The company launched in 2018 with their friend Xavier Payan, who studied wine and spirits management alongside Cosculluela.
During pandemic lockdowns, while the rest of us dusted off gaming consoles or mined the more questionable parts of Netflix’s catalog, Picard sharpened her skills gained as a spirits development project manager at barrel-maker Demptos to research a more scientific approach to whisky-making—one that leaned far less heavily on barrel aging for flavor and instead looked to molecular science, sensory analysis, and copious amounts of data. At the time, Picard even posted her progress online as an open logbook of her experiments.
The conclusion Picard and Cosculluela came to after these experiments was this: a great spirit is decided at fermentation, not by age. “Whisky makers are very focused on the style of cask. It's not our vision,” says Picard.
“What we try to do is not increase the production but focus on the quality of the whisky, and more precisely on the steps before the maturation,” Picard says. “We worked on the quality of the wash—the liquid issued from the fermentation, just like in the wine industry. We worked a lot on techniques used in the wine industry. For example, the use of lactic bacteria during the fermentation, and the use of lees aging—which is a process used for champagne or Chardonnay wines to increase the rawness.”
Before fermentation, organic French barley is cold-soaked to bring out its brighter notes. Then there’s a long, seven-day fermentation that builds flavor (compared with a typical two or three days for scotch). The addition of lees aging keeps the Lineti wash in contact with the fermentation process's dead yeast cells for a full two weeks to develop more floral and fruity aromas.
Picard also employs malolactic fermentation, a secondary winemaking process where lactic acid bacteria convert sharp, tart malic acids into softer, creamier lactic acids. Such a process wouldn't be allowed in scotch production, which is strictly regulated, but EU law permits such manipulation. In wine, the process would result in a softer texture, but in Lineti's whisky, along with that creamier mouthfeel, it adds length and even more floral notes.
Maison Lineti’s wine-based, science-laden fermentation process happens in the “egg box”—a remarkable space housing seven giant concrete, egg-shaped fermenters that reach to the ceiling. Cosculluela says the concrete allows for precise temperature control, as the material much thicker than the stainless steel that’s typically used. Additionally, the lack of internal ridges in the eggs supposedly make for better movement and churn of the liquid when the yeasts are fermenting.
The tangible gains from all this work before the fruits of their labor go into barrels are not merely limited to improved and distinctive flavor profiles. Cosculluela claims that Maison Lineti’s pre-maturation may well take weeks longer than other makers, but, crucially, it saves two to four years of barrel aging. This is how Maison Lineti’s relatively young whisky somewhat magically goes toe-to-toe with single malt scotch that is many years older. (Which it does. Take our word for it.)
It also means Cosculluela and Picard end up with more booze for their buck. A faster maturation to a minimum viable product, if you will, means the angels get to steal less of Maison Lineti’s produce. The “angel’s share” is the portion of whisky that naturally evaporates through the porous wood of the casks into the atmosphere during the spirit’s aging process. Simply put, less time in Lineti’s barrels means less whisky disappears.
“Every year you lose 2 percent of your whisky, so you need to produce approximately 20 percent more than the final volume you will need at 10 years,” Cosculluela says. “So if you work on the drinkability to get something really tasty and balanced in three years, you save a lot of raw material, a lot of space in your warehouse, and a lot of energy.”
However, for Picard, this use of these winemaking skills and methods is not enough to ensure success for Maison Linetti—comprehensive data analysis is also key. Excel files document some 10,000 lines of data per batch produced.
“On the brewing part, we collect temperature, the time, the transfer yield of the pump, the water added, everything,” Cosculluela says. “For the fermentation, we collect the time and temperature every 20 minutes. For the stills, we have the ABV, the temperature, and the speed.” As a result, Cosculluela and Picard can see the direct impacts of any changes they make. “We try to change only one parameter at a time,” Cosculluela says, so that any improvements can be tracked back to exactly what was altered.
“If we develop a project on the fermentation parts, we just need a different samples from the batch, and you can collect the data in two weeks,” says Picard. “But do a study on the maturation? That needs time. We conducted one three years ago, and we've only just begun to have the final results.”
The data science isn't the only thing that's been an arduous process for Maison Lineti. Cosculluela and Picard have been tested financially, too. In July last year, after all their hard work, experiments, and graft, the company was forced into liquidation when its main wine-producing backer withdrew from the business. However, before the worst could happen, Maison Lineti secured a new unnamed investor, a French entrepreneur who, fittingly, apparently made their fortune in the luxury industry.
This new injection of cash has resulted in, just this week, Maison Lineti's whisky going on sale to the public in the UK for the first time. The intention, Cosculluela says, is to bring the spirit to the US in 2028. The launch range consists of a core expression, called Calibre No1, sitting alongside two limited editions, named “Complications,” all three clearly referencing the luxury watchmaking world in their nomenclature.
At 47.7 percent ABV, Calibre No1 single malt is WIRED's clear favorite, and the most accessible at £50 (about $67) for 70 cl (about 23.7 fluid ounces). It’s described as the DNA of the brand—sophisticated, complex, and elegant. Complication No1 is matured in ex-bourbon casks and is limited to 850 bottles. It is more focused on the malolactic fermentation, and it proposes something different altogether, in no way trying to compete with the distilleries of Scotland or elsewhere. Complication No2 is limited to 750 bottles and is all about offering a profile defined by Oloroso sherry casks. All of these whiskies are just three and a half years old, but, quite remarkably, taste much more mature.
Drinks writer and presenter Becky Paskin, who is also the former editor of The Spirits Business and Scotchwhisky.com, is unequivocal in her praise of what Maison Lineti has managed to achieve. “What they're doing is probably the most innovative thing to happen to whisky in decades,” Paskin says. “By leaning on their own background and oenology, they've created whisky that is completely unique … for now. Other producers around the world will look to what they're doing and potentially start to use some of these techniques.”
As for the undeniably subtle and interesting flavors Cosculluela and Picard are managing to conjure, Paskin thinks the whiskey world is only beginning to see the distillery's potential. "You're only just starting to see the tip of what Maison Lineti is capable of. They've got all these levers they can pull. So, ultimately, we could see very creamy, very fruity whiskies. We could see whiskies that are more malty in character, but they always have this signature floral undertone. Every distillery needs a DNA, and that's what's unique to Maison Lineti.”
The World Whisky Forum's Dave Broom, who has also written 14 books on the spirit, agrees. “I am very excited by what what has come out, but more excited by what is going to come out,” he says. “In terms of flavor production, interaction between between wood and air and spirit, down to a molecular level—that is innovation, and genuinely groundbreaking. I think [Maison Lineti] is one of the most important distilleries in the world at the moment.”

articles.title: How long is too long for a USB cable? - Engadget
articles.text:
How long is too long for a USB cable?
One of the best things about USB is that you rarely need to think about it. Sure, there are some differences between USB generations, but no matter what, if you plug a USB cable into a compatible device, it will work without issues, as long as the cable isn't too long, that is. Of course, you're unlikely to need an extremely lengthy USB cable — unlike, say, HDMI cables — but if you ever do, there are limits to USB cable length that you should be aware of.
The USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF), which defines USB standards, has outlined maximum lengths for different types of USB cables. These range from about 16 feet to as low as 3 feet. The Forum is an industry group, not a regulatory body, so there's nothing stopping manufacturers from making longer cables. The limits are a guide to best practices, as exceeding the USB-IF's specifications could hamper a USB cable's performance.
USB transfer speeds suffer with longer cables
Each generation of USB cables can transfer data faster than the last, but later generations actually have a shorter recommended length. USB 1.0 and 2.0 cables have a recommended maximum of 16.4 feet. For USB 3.0 through 3.2, that drops to 9.8 feet. USB 4 cables are much more limited, with a maximum recommended length of just 2.6 feet. Whether you're using a USB-A or USB-C cable doesn't matter; the maximum length is the same either way.
It might seem odd that maximum cable length doesn't improve over time as transfer rate does, but it has to do with the physical limits of the cables. A signal traveling through a cable degrades over time due to electrical resistance. The farther a signal has to travel, the more cable it has to push through to get there, losing signal along the way. Longer cables are also more susceptible to damage, which can further slow transfer speeds.
A USB cable that's too long won't suddenly stop working. Instead, it simply won't function as well as one that's within spec. Data may transfer more slowly than you're used to, or connected devices won't receive as much power. The higher the potential transfer rate or power delivery, the more you're likely to notice the difference. That's why it's important to know the maximum length of your USB cables.
How to extend the range of a USB cable
If you can, it's always best to reposition your devices so you don't need to exceed a USB cable's length limits, but that's not always possible. In those cases, you can purchase an active USB cable or an active USB extender, either of which will have built-in components to extend the signal's range. However, active USB cables are significantly more expensive than standard cables. They also draw extra power from the USB port, and thus might not be compatible with older ports.
Another potential solution is to use a powered USB hub and use the longest supported cable between the hub and your computer. Plugging too many devices into the same hub can slow them down, but as long as you don't exceed the USB port's bandwidth, you shouldn't encounter any noticeable performance difference. Powered hubs are preferable, since an unpowered hub can only draw power from the USB port, which can be unreliable.

articles.title: My Fridge Is Ready for the Next Power Outage
articles.text:
Seamless failover when power cuts out. Discreet; disappears almost completely behind your fridge. Reasonably mobile; can conceivably be used for other needs in a pinch.
TIRED
Scheduling system is very basic. No logging system to speak of. Installation is tougher than it seems. (Learn from my mistakes!) Very costly; TOU rate-shifting benefits are minimal.
Every part of a power outage is always a massive nuisance, but nothing is quite as aggravating as losing power to your refrigerator and the resultant spoilage of everything inside it.
Homes with a whole-house battery backup can avoid this headache, but the cost for a system like a Tesla Powerwall can easily hit $15,000 after installation. It takes an awful lot of melted ice cream for those numbers to balance out.
BioLite—known for its range of lighting and portable power solutions—is on the cusp of launching an alternative to whole-house batteries. Backup by BioLite is a modular battery system designed specifically with the fridge in mind, offering long-term emergency power at a fraction of the cost of more complex systems and which homeowners can install themselves. I installed it in my home and found it a capable (if limited) way to get a little extra peace of mind.
Smart Cells
Backup by BioLite is hardly a difficult concept to grasp. The massive battery—offering 1526 watt-hours of power with a rated output of 1800 watts (and supporting peak surges up to 3000 watts)—mounts on the wall behind your refrigerator, or it can simply sit on top of it. The power pack measures 29 inches high by 13 inches wide, and a single unit weighs a hefty 40 pounds. No special wiring is required. You simply plug the Backup into a standard 120-volt outlet, then plug your refrigerator into the Backup.
Want more power? Backup’s Core unit can be daisy-chained to a Backup Extend add-on device, an identically sized (but slightly lighter) unit that doubles the power capacity to 3072 Wh.
Depending on your refrigerator, the full “Backup Complete” solution, with two cells, can provide up to 60 hours of running time if the grid goes down. If that’s not enough, additional Backup Extend devices can be added in series, with a total maximum capacity of 10.5 KWh. (Though, at that point, you may as well spring for a whole-house solution.)
DIY Time
One of the biggest selling points of Backup by BioLite is that you can install it yourself, with no electrician. I’ve got no trouble wielding a drill, so I undertook the effort to see if BioLite’s promise of a 30-minute install would pan out. I tested Backup Complete, with two Backup batteries situated side by side.
The process seems straightforward (and is enhanced by a helpful printed manual), but I quickly learned that my refrigerator’s location—tucked into an alcove—would complicate things because of the limited space in which to work. BioLite suggests having an extra pair of hands to hoist the heavy battery packs into place, but there was simply no room for my wife to squeeze into the alcove to help with any of the process. I managed on my own, but I expect this will present a challenge for some.
The batteries mount to metal brackets, and BioLite provides a template to help you position them properly and ensure they are level. It’s essential that the two batteries in a Backup Complete arrangement be located at a specific distance from one another, as the cable that connects the two is limited in length.
I dutifully chose a location for the template, ensuring that the batteries—once attached to the wall—would not block access to the electrical outlet. Since my outlet is placed 3 feet off the ground, that meant hanging the batteries high, with the tops level with my eyeline.
Photograph: Christopher Null
BioLite provides all the hardware you need to mount the units in drywall, including anchors and screws. I tried to find a stud to anchor at least one of the screws, but found none in the spots where I needed them. Oddly, I had to use my own drywall anchors for some of the screws, as BioLite’s screw-in style anchors refused to engage and drive into the wall. (I don’t blame BioLite for this but rather some peculiarity with how that section of wall was constructed.)
With holes drilled and anchors set, I carefully attached the metal brackets to the wall. Everything looked level and sturdy, at which point I heaved the first of the massive batteries into place. Or, at least, I tried to. Turns out, I’d made a massive mistake. My idea was to mount the bracket so the Core battery was flush with the right-hand wall, but unfortunately, the Backup template isn’t designed with enough buffer space on each side of the brackets. The batteries stick out well beyond the sides of the brackets and a bit beyond the template; in my case, with the template flush with the wall, the battery pushed up against the wall and was unable to properly seat atop the bracket. Even if it had, it wouldn’t have mattered: The outlets for the Core battery are on its right side, so you need another few inches to make room to plug things into it (and to scan the QR code printed there during setup).
All of that is a long way of saying that BioLite simply needs to make its template larger to account for the extra room needed on the right side of the device. It’s also a long way for me to say that I then had to disassemble the brackets and redo the entire thing, shifting everything left a few inches.
Photograph: Christopher Null
With my brackets finally repositioned, I was able to mount the batteries on them. The shape of the cells and their lack of handholds makes them a little awkward to wrestle into place—particularly after my earlier mishaps with the misplaced brackets—but once I had them hanging where they were supposed to be, secured with a single screw on the underside of the bracket, everything felt amply secure. The entire process took about 90 minutes.
With all that said, if I had to do it again, I’d strongly consider just dropping the batteries on top of the fridge instead of bothering with the wall mount, a setup fully endorsed by BioLite. This would save a lot of time and headache, and this design would make them far easier to move elsewhere in case of future emergencies.
Energized
After plugging everything in, the batteries begin charging automatically. Some status lights on the left side of each battery indicate charge level, but these were hard to see, especially after pushing the fridge back into place. (I also noted that my fridge is no longer flush with the wall, now sticking out a couple extra inches due to the added hardware behind it.)
Photograph: Christopher Null
Before replacing the fridge, I made sure I had the app setup. As noted earlier, BioLite’s Backup app requires you to scan a QR code on the side of the battery, but after that it’s a fairly quick jog through pairing the units with your phone, then bridging them to connect to your home Wi-Fi network. A firmware update then started, during which my refrigerator was without power, though this only took a few minutes.
While the Backup app is intuitive and easy to use, I was a little surprised by how simplistic it is—perhaps overly so. Front and center, you’ll see some basic stats: Battery charge level, and energy input and output levels—including whether you are drawing from the battery or the grid. If you have solar power (I don’t), this is split from grid power input so you can track usage types. If you have multiple Backup batteries, you can drill down to see the battery life remaining for each.
BioLite has done a generally great job with Backup’s emergency power features. When I cut the input power manually by tripping the circuit breaker, the battery kicked in immediately and without delay. Batteries draw down roughly equally, ensuring that over time they’ll be taxed at about the same rate. (BioLite specs that after 4,000 cycles, total capacity should remain at 80 percent of each battery’s original maximum.)
What’s missing? When the power goes out, there’s no audible alarm or other notification, except for a push notification that’s sent to your app. An alarm option would be helpful, as would a notification when power is restored. As it stands, the only way to know if the power is on is to check the app to see where output to the refrigerator is coming from. It also looks like BioLite’s estimate of my backup time (“a day”) is overly optimistic. Based on my refrigerator’s average draw of 170 watts, I expect I’d have on the order of 18 hours of reserve power, which BioLite’s app should be able to easily calculate. (That said, I have avoided running the batteries down to zero, as I wanted to preserve their longevity.)
ScreenshotBioLite Backup app via Christopher Null
ScreenshotBioLite Backup app via Christopher Null
As with all home batteries, there’s some bonus value in Backup to be found in running the battery when there’s not a power outage. That’s because you can take advantage of Time of Use (TOU) rate billing from your utility, running off of battery power during peak times when rates are high (usually the afternoon and evening), and drawing from the grid and recharging the batteries when rates are low. I had to do some research to find out if my utility provider even offered TOU billing, as I’ve had a conventional, static rate plan since we moved into this house four years ago. Turns out they did, and I promptly switched over to the new one to give this a try.
It’s easy to set up a battery schedule in the Backup app: Just set the time each day you want the battery to kick in and the time for it to switch back to grid power under the Scheduling tab. Charging can be paused during certain times of the day as well, and you can set a lower limit for how far the batteries can drain. Weekends can be excluded from all of this at your discretion.
Unfortunately, that’s it: You can’t set multiple on/off cycles during the day (my provider has two peak disconnected billing times during the winter, so this would have been nice), nor can you set different schedules for different times of year (again, my provider has three different billing schedules, depending on the month). If you’re going to spend thousands of dollars on backup batteries, it would be useful to be able to really fine-tune how they’re used. I did encounter one bug when trying to save the schedule, but a quick force-quit and restart ultimately got everything working fine.
The other missing feature is a log. Power nerds like me would love to see how long the battery ran each day, how much power was used during each run, how much power it required to recharge it, and potentially how much money was saved. Unfortunately, there’s no logging system at all in the Backup app aside from a simple record of when outages happened along with any errors or updates.
It’s easy to do the rough math on how much money I’m now saving. For the fall, I am able to shift four hours (5 to 9 pm) of refrigerator running time that would normally cost 8.6 cents per kWh to the BioLite batteries, which recharge after hours at 4.3 cents per kWh. While the numbers are surely imperfect due to the vagaries of energy loss among these various components, I’m now able to move 680 Wh of usage from the higher rate to the lower rate each day. Total savings: 3 cents per day, or about a dollar a month. That’s admittedly not very impressive, but in the summer months, the peak usage rate here hits 16.2 cents per kWh, moving monthly savings up to three dollars each month.
OK, still not that impressive, but not nothing.
A Costly Life Vest
One final feature of note is that BioLite ships the unit with a power strip, complete with an optional magnetic backing that lets you slap it onto the side of your fridge. This power strip attaches to a second outlet on the Backup and can be used to connect additional devices to your battery backup system. The power strip is totally optional, but it’s a capable product, with three standard outlets, two USB-A, and two USB-C plugs. Ultimately, I didn’t use it because I didn’t have anywhere convenient to place it, and nothing to plug into it anyway, but it’s a nice-to-have feature that I’ll hold onto in case the power cuts out this winter and I want to run other devices in the dark. With 1800 watts of output, the battery is strong enough to power everything from a microwave oven to an air fryer.
That’s just a small bonus to push the value of Backup by BioLite a bit further into sanity because at $1,999 for a single battery and $3,499 for the pair, the math isn’t easy to justify. Realistically, the real benefit to the system comes almost entirely from its use in case of emergency, protecting what could be hundreds of dollars of groceries from spoiling because of a random ice storm—and making it possible to cook them, too, even if the lights in the rest of the house are out.
Christopher Null, a longtime technology journalist, is a contributor to WIRED and the editor of Drinkhacker. Chris is among our lead laptop reviewers and leads WIRED's coverage of hearing aids.
